Boise State shaping up to be the conference leader despite hanging on in the conference game of the year (so far). One would think that this late in the season a college football team wouldn’t be having to deal with quarterback issues. Usually with an injury, the player returns to resume his position when he is physically able. This is not that usual situation. Coach Sean Lewis and staff will have a week of practice to evaluate whether they continue with successful backup Stone Saunders or a healthy Jayden Denegal when he returns. While Denegal has struggled on what seems a weekly basis, Saunders has had three very impressive performances closing out a win against Fresno State, a close loss to Colorado State and a slugfest against Washington State.. His line for the season so far is 43 of 69 passing attempts for 552 yards and a 62.3% completion percentage. His average yards per pass is 8 yards and he’s thrown two touchdowns against three interceptions. He is more of a typical drop back passer, but has the ability to escape a rush and he will choose to get rid of the ball instead of running. This is different than Denegal, who has a 55% completion percentage on 93 of 151 passing attempts for 899 yards. He has thrown seven touchdowns against five interceptions. Denegal has been ineffective in most of his outings, just lacking the spark to drive consistency. Saunders, meanwhile, has realistic expectations attached to a freshman. He has missed some targets, but has shown the ability to stretch the field with longer passes and establish consistency on his short to midrange targets. One knock against the Aztecs this season has been their inability to move the chains, especially on third down. Saunders has been impressive, capturing a 52.4% conversion rate compared to 29.4% when Denegal is under center. This week will be important for Saunders as practice reps with the first team are premium quality snaps. item.description: Angel Reese and Karl Smesko. | NBAE via Getty Images The Atlanta Dream were about 10 minutes away from becoming WNBA champions. Before that, they tied the franchise record for wins a single season. They won a playoff series for the first time since 2018. Across the end of the regular season and into the playoffs, they won a franchise-record 10 games in a row. Also, they won a Finals game for the first time in team history, and notched two more to advance to the first Game 7 in WNBA history. And, again, they were a Gabby Williams explosion away from winning it. It was, undoubtedly, the most successful season in team history. So, why did it happen? And, what’s next? Here’s a look back at the Dream’s 2026 season. In the comments, be sure to share your perspective. Atlanta has entered and embraced their Angel Era The acquisition of Angel Reese, obviously, drove the Dream to new heights. While her impact exceeded the boundaries of the basketball court, as Angel almost instantly became one of the most culturally influential athletes in Atlanta sports history, she was still more impactful on the court, elevating the Dream with her competitive mentality as she put together a Defensive Player of the Year-winning and Second Team All-WNBA-worthy season. While they were talking, she was working. Now, she sits at the top as your 2026 WNBA DPOY 🙌 And this is only the beginning. pic.twitter.com/1SUiwR5CAl — Atlanta Dream (@AtlantaDream) October 1, 2026 Throughout the season, Angel kept getting better, and so did Atlanta. The ascent appeared unstoppable. After the first three games of the Finals, it seemed that Reese’s relentless rise wasn’t going to stop until she had her hands on two pieces of hardware: the championship and Finals MVP trophies. The final four games of the series, however, showed that Angel’s greatness was not immune to the gravity of the game. The history of pro basketball reminds that trials, tribulations and tough moments are prerequisites to the ultimate triumph. Reese could never rediscover her dominant rhythm, particularly struggling in Game 7. Angel, however, has always demonstrated an acute understanding of her limitations, in addition to an unmatched motivation to overcome them. item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 31: Hoosier the bison Indiana mascot drives an Indy car onto the field prior to a college football game between the Minnesota Golden Gophers and Indiana Hoosiers on October 31, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The first set of College Football Playoff rankings were released on Tuesday night and boy oh boy are they generating some discussions . There isn’t really an unstoppable-looking juggernaut in the sport this season, with a few teams sitting with undefeated records but just two of said teams in the top-4. They aren’t even 1-2! Then, of course, there’s Indiana sitting at No. 4, which is higher than I and several others expected them to be. Let’s dig into that. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android for coverage of the Hoosiers and all your favorite teams! Indiana’s strength of record is stronger than most think Indiana owns no ranked wins on the season at this point. To a casual observer, this is a glaring sign of schedule weakness. That’s not the case though. The Hoosiers have beaten six opponents with a winning record this season, five of which came in Big Ten play. Indiana’s Big Ten wins, in schedule order, rank in at No. 23, No. 96, No. 26, No. 29 and No. 59 in SP+. It’s prevailed over SP+‘s No. 10, No. 4 and No. 28th rated defenses, being a few inches away from doing so against the No. 3 rated defense and owning the No. 1 rated defense to itself. Are the margins slim? Yes. But wins are wins! Indiana’s strength of record sits at No. 4 nationally in ESPN’s Football Power Index, just behind UCLA, Kentucky and Miami. So about “quality losses”… Indiana’s sole loss on the 2026 season came at home against Ohio State, which sits eight spots below the Hoosiers at No. 12 in the rankings after suffering road losses at No. 7 Texas and No. 20 USC. The Hoosiers, as previously mentioned, were a few inches shy of beating the Buckeyes. The nature of the loss probably factored into Indiana’s first ranking, as did those of No. 2 Georgia to unranked Auburn and No. 5 Alabama to Georgia and No. 13 Tennessee. If you don’t punish Georgia, almost at all, for losing to an unranked opponent or you can’t really justify doing so for Indiana losing to Ohio State. Much less Alabama losing to two ranked foes and ending up right behind the Hoosiers anyway. The Hoosiers have some control over their ultimate playoff fate Indiana has three games left in 2026 and the opportunity to pick up a ranked win at home over USC with both teams coming off of a bye week. After that it’s Washington on the road and Purdue at home. It isn’t impossible to see Indiana falling to USC dropping in the rankings nor winning out and somehow still losing out on a top-4 spot. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears looks on before introductions against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images In front of a national audience, once again, the Chicago Bears defeated a conference champion. This time in the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Considering the Bears are on the verge of a certain level of success the franchise hasn’t experienced in decades thanks to Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, I am going to leave them out of this piece from now on – as it is a given that both were instrumental to Chicago’s success. Instead, I will be highlighting 3 other factors that contributed to Chicago’s win or loss. So let’s get to it. 1. Jeffery Simmons Simply put: Simmons was a game-wrecker Monday night. The way he stepped in and made an immediate impact was reminiscent of Khalil Mack’s Bears Intro back in 2018. Except Chicago won in dominating fashion this time around. Simmons presence was felt and it was noticeable when he was off the field. By now, we have all seen the stats showing that the Seahawks averaged close to 3 years per play when he was on the field compared to 13+ when he was off it, but the way he changed how Dennis Allen called this game was what fascinated me the most. The Bears came into MNF averaging a 40% blitz rate. Against Seattle, they cut that down to 15%…and their pressure rate *went up.* Discussed the Jeffrey Simmons effect with @BenjaminSolak 👇 pic.twitter.com/hHizP5a6iF — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) November 3, 2026 Jeffery Simmons’ mere presence allowed Dennis Allen to keep more defenders in coverage while simultaneously occupying the attention of more offensive linemen. This allowed guys like Devin Bush, Montez Sweat and Austin Booker to really shine in ways we have not seen. item.description: The Arizona Cardinals are trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, guaranteeing that he won’t be the starter when the Los Angeles Rams face them next week. The Rams lost to Brissett’s Cardinals 18-16 just 17 days ago, but now Arizona is turning to Gardner Minshew for the rest of the season with Carson Beck as the backup. The Ravens are in need of a quarterback after losing both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in a matter of one half of football. Brissett struggled so badly against the Cowboys defense on Sunday that Mike LaFleur benched him for Minshew in the second half, and then Minshew led the Cardinals to an overtime win. Minshew will now be starting for his sixth career NFL team. The Cardinals had to give Brissett a raise this season — up to $21 million — because he wanted to be paid like a starter. item.title: Liverpool handed first defeat of Champions League campaign
item.description: Liverpool handed first defeat of Champions League campaign Liverpool twice surrendered the lead as Fenerbahce inflicted a 3-2 Champions League defeat on Andoni Iraola’s side in Istanbul. Trey Nyoni put Liverpool ahead after 25 minutes with his first senior goal, finishing from the edge of the box after the visitors had made a promising start. But the advantage lasted only four minutes, with Mason Greenwood’s deflected free-kick beating Alisson to bring Fenerbahce level. Iraola turned to his bench after the break and was rewarded when Alexander Isak restored Liverpool’s lead in the 69th minute, finishing from Cody Gakpo’s assist shortly after being introduced. Archie Brown equalised for Fenerbahce four minutes later before striker Vedat Muriqi headed the hosts in front in the 79th minute to complete the turnaround. Liverpool were unable to find another response as their winning start to the Champions League campaign came to an end after three successive victories.

item.title: Eagles switching to QB Giants fans wanted when Jaxson Dart was injured
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III warms up | Getty Images It appears as though the Philadelphia Eagles are throwing a curveball at the New York Giants. The Eagles have decided to make a change at quarterback and are starting quarterback Joe Milton III, per a report from Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport . The report comes as the Giants have spent much of the last week since their upset win over the Houston Texans preparing for Tanner McKee. McKee has started the last three games for the Eagles and is 0-3 in that stretch, completing 63.2 percent of his passes with 2 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. The Eagles have lost their last three games by a combined 45-90. Milton III was originally drafted by the New England Patriots out of Tennessee in the 6th round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He was traded to the Dallas Cowboys in the spring of 2025, and the Eagles signed him off the Dallas practice squad on October 16th. Where McKee is a relatively immobile pocket passer, Milton is a massive (6-foot-5, 236-pound), athletic, and strong-armed quarterback. Milton has appeared in five games in 2024 and 2025, but only saw significant action in the Patriots’ 2024-2025 Week 18 win over the Buffalo Bills. Milton didn’t start, but finished that game 22 of 29 for 241 yards and a touchdown. It was a shockingly good performance, and one he has yet to replicate. While Milton possesses elite physical tools, he was heavily knocked for inconsistency and a lack of accuracy in college. He has enough arm strength to access all areas of the field, but completed just 38.6% of his passes beyond 10 yards downfield — despite Tennessee’s simplistic offense. He also rarely threw with anything like timing, touch, or anticipation and is much more of a “fastball only” passer. That said, Milton’s presence will force the Giants’ pass rush to be more disciplined. He’s a powerful and fast runner, which could hurt the Giants if they’re undisciplined in their rushes or allow him to break contain. It will be interesting to see how the Giants adapt to the sudden change at quarterback, and whether Milton can spark a listless Eagles’ offense.

item.title: ‘He was throwing deli meat out there’: Rams safety says ‘I don’t know what’s going on’ with Justin Herbert
item.description: Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images It’s been a miserable season for quarterback Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers. And opponents aren’t holding back when talking about it. Los Angeles is still looking for its first win after a loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. In the loss, Herbert threw two interceptions, and one Rams defender who picked off Herbert in that game didn’t hold back when describing what he saw on film. ‘He was throwing deli meat out there’ Rams safety Quentin Lake joined Amon-Ra and Equanimeous St. Brown on the latest episode of the St. Brown Podcast , where he was asked about his interception of Herbert in the Rams’ 24-9 win. “I mean, he was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said. “Was he, bro?” one of the St. Brown brothers asked. “He’s seeing ghosts,” Lake said. “I don’t know what’s going on, but like we knew we were going to get a couple. Like, that was, we knew we were going to at least one.” The Rams got their couple. Lake returned his interception 45 yards, and Trent McDuffie added another. Herbert finished 24-of-32 for 257 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. He now has 10 interceptions on the season. The Chargers are in trouble The loss dropped the Chargers to 0-7. They’ve scored just 99 points this season, the fewest in the NFL. Herbert has taken plenty of heat during the losing streak. Last month, Jim Harbaugh blamed some of Herbert’s struggles on “desperation time.” This week, Emmanuel Acho suggested Herbert needs LASIK , saying. “Either Herbert is invested in the opponent, either Herbert is gambling on the opponent, or Herbert simply cannot see,” Acho argued. Needless to say, it’s a far cry from the expectations Jim Harbaugh set for his quarterback before the season when he predicted Herbert “will be known as the greatest, best ever to play the position of quarterback.” The Chargers will try again for their first win on Sunday when they host the Texans. Houston’s defense will surely be hoping for some deli meat of its own. item.title: Liverpool collapse to Champions League defeat at Fenerbahce
item.description: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner as Fenerbahce beat Liverpool (YASIN AKGUL) Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign. Liverpool had won their opening three European games under Andoni Iraola, but were punished for sloppy defending in a surprise defeat. Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front. But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi's winner. Fenerbahce's interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week. The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool's generosity at the back. Liverpool's perfect Champions League start allowed Iraola the luxury of leaving out Isak and Florian Wirtz among five changes from Sunday's 1-0 defeat by Arsenal. Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box. Just four minutes later, though, Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood's deflected free-kick to equalise. Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark and got an almost immediate reward. Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo's cross. But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage. Gakpo's touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post. Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner. Defeat cost Liverpool the chance to move level with Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table as they sit. Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table. kca/jc

item.title: ‘Soft’ – Stephen Warnock takes aim at Liverpool star who ‘cost his side’ against Fenerbahce
item.description: ‘Soft’ – Stephen Warnock takes aim at Liverpool star who ‘cost his side’ against Fenerbahce Stephen Warnock was critical of one Liverpool player over the concession of a ‘soft goal’ in their Champions League clash against Fenerbahce on Wednesday. The Reds had the lead twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium, with Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak netting for Andoni Iraola’s side, but the midfielder’s goal was swiftly cancelled out by a deflected Mason Greenwood free kick . The home side equalised again through Archie Brown and had the final say with a Vedat Muriqi header which secured all three points. Warnock blames Alisson for Fenerbahce equaliser The second Fenerbahce goal had Warnock pointing the finger of blame at Alisson Becker for not coming to claim the ball from the cross which led to the left-back’s leveller. Speaking on MOTD: UEFA Champions League for BBC Sport , the former Liverpool defender said: “That’s another soft goal conceded by Liverpool but this one was more down to Alisson not coming to claim the ball – and either cleaning out Gakpo or letting him know he is coming. “I just watched the replay and there was definitely no shout… that’s a lack of concentration from the goalkeeper, and it has cost his side.” Image via TNT Sports Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust It wasn’t just Alisson who did poorly on Brown’s goal Alisson had bailed out his teammates a couple of times earlier in the match after some sloppy errors just outside the penalty area, but the goalkeeper won’t be happy with his involvement in Brown’s equaliser. He was unusually hesitant in coming for the ball as the cross was played in, although he doesn’t bear sole culpability for a cheap goal for Fenerbahce. Cody Gakpo was unlucky that his attempted headed clearance went backwards, but Dominik Szoboszlai completely switched off to allow the left-back to run in behind him and have a simple finish from close range. It was a collective mess-up from Liverpool, who could also have done a lot more to prevent Muriqi from scoring what proved to be the winner for Dirk Kuyt’s side. It’s now two defeats in a row to begin November for the Reds, but they’re still in a healthy position to advance to the round of 16 in the Champions League, having won their three previous games in the tournament.

item.title: Caddix comes to the defense of Caleb Williams following cleats fine
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Caddix comes to the defense of Caleb Williams following cleats fine appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chicago Bears QB Caleb Williams has been pretty defiant lately. Not just on the field, but in the cleats he laces up. Specifically, Williams wears cleats made by Caddix, a company Jack Rasmussen founded in 2023. Because the NFL hasn’t approved the brand, the league fined Williams . According to ESPN, Williams accumulated $35,823 in fines. The cleats displayed an unauthorized logo, as the league has partnerships with Nike, Adidas, and Under Armor. On Monday, Williams wore plain black cleats during the Bears’ victory over the Seattle Seahawks . Meanwhile, Williams says he still will wear the cleats to prevent injuries. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) On Wednesday, Michelle Kafka, COO and Account Director at Kafka Media Group, which handles Caddix’s PR, defended Williams in a statement to ClutchPoints. “It’s unprecedented for a player like Caleb Williams to not have a shoe deal or contract with a shoe brand. Typically, the first all-around draft pick in the NFL would have a deal prior to ever stepping foot on the field. In addition to that, Williams is choosing to wear a brand that isn’t paying him and has no league affiliation. All of what he’s doing is why it’s causing such a large conversation around athlete branding and safety. This moment and fine points to an overall issue with a league-wide deal on a logo. Athletes technically have a choice with which brand they sign with or wear, but they aren’t allowed to show logos that their league doesn’t approve. We see this in NFL, NSWL, NBA, across all sports athletes are given a choice but still have to abide by only showing what their league dictates.” Caddix cleats include “SmartStuds” technology, which aims to prevent lower body injuries. item.title: Lions' Campbell has movement in lower body after neck injury
item.description: Jack Campbell remained on the ground after being injured on a play against the Minnesota Vikings (Mike Mulholland) Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell said Wednesday he has full movement in his lower body and is making progress in his upper body after suffering a neck injury during last weekend's NFL game. Campbell remained lying face down on the floor after making a tackle in the Lions' clash with Minnesota, was carted off the field, and has remained hospitalized since. After the team said signs were positive for Campbell's recovery, the 26-year-old player expressed optimism about his progress in a statement issued via the Lions' social media. "I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," said Campbell. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." Speaking to media later Wednesday, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said receiving the update direct from his player "means a lot". "That's powerful in itself. You know, more than hearing it from me or anybody else. Those are his and his family's words, so that's powerful," he said. "That always helps to know that he's improving, because at this point that's all you're looking for, is just to know that he is improving," said Campbell. "This thing, the status is changing every eight hours, 10 hours, in a good way." The 26-year-old from Iowa was a first-round selection in the 2023 NFL Draft by the Lions, chosen 18th overall. Campbell had a career-best season for Detroit in 2025 with 89 solo tackles, five sacks and 176 combined tackles. He also forced three fumbles and recovered two. The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension worth $81 million. The injury occurred during Detroit's 19-15 NFL victory Sunday over previously unbeaten Minnesota. item.description: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni stands on the field before a NFL preseason football game against the Miami Dolphins, Saturday, Aug. 27, 2022, in Miami Gardens, Fla. (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky) The Philadelphia Eagles have made a quarterback change. Philadelphia will start Joe Milton on Sunday against the New York Giants and are benching Tanner McKee, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Mike Garafolo. The Eagles signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. The Steelers play the Eagles in Week 12 at Lincoln Financial Field. It appears that Milton will get the nod for that game, as well. The Eagles have a bye week before their game against Pittsburgh. Philadelphia has been a house of horrors for the Steelers , as they haven’t won in the City of Brotherly Love since 1965 (11 games in a row). Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. McKee lost all three starts after Hurts was sidelined. The Eagles have lost six straight after starting the season 2-0. It’s the first time since 1999 that the Eagles have started 2-6. A QB change in Philadelphia: the Eagles are naming Joe Milton their starting QB and benching Tanner McKee for Sunday’s game vs. the Giants, per @mikegarafolo and me. pic.twitter.com/kVkMqLmUb4 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 4, 2026 The New England Patriots selected Milton in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. In his only extended NFL action in Week 18 of 2024 vs. Buffalo, Milton completed 22 of 29 passes for 241 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 111.4 in a 23-18 win over the Bills. Buffalo already clinched a playoff spot, so they had their backups in. The Patriots traded Milton to the Cowboys along with a 2025 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2025 fifth-round pick in April 2025. Milton, who stands at 6-foot-5, 235 pounds, was lauded for his elite athleticism coming into the NFL. He was also tabbed as very raw, however. “Rare physical specimen with the proverbial “arm talent to make all the NFL throws,” but he’s prevented from doing so by a lack of timing, accuracy and touch. Milton is gifted with a cannon for a right arm and can throw the ball as hard or as far as you want. His fastballs are often inaccurate and difficult to catch for moving targets, and he was wildly inconsistent locating his deep throws,” Lance Zierlein of NFL.com wrote in a scouting report. “He can elude pressure, extend plays and put jaw-dropping highlights on tape, but he’s never been able to mature his game from splashy to consistent.
